pages.text: Reefer cargo claims have come from mixing up plus and minus temperatures. On a thermometer, count down past 0 and the numbers keep going. Below zero are the [[negative numbers]].

pages.name: Find −3
pages.task: Where does −3 go? Slide it to its place on the line.
pages.why: −3 means 3 below zero. Start at 0 and count 3 steps down, to −1, −2 and then −3.

pages.alt: An upright number line from 2 down to minus 10, with an arrow up the side marked bigger. Minus 2 is marked, and minus 7 lower down. Brackets show minus 2 is 2 below zero and minus 7 is 7 below zero.

pages.text: On the line, higher up is bigger. −2 sits above −7, so −2 is bigger. The bigger the number after the minus, the further below zero it sits.

pages.name: Which is warmer?
pages.task: Slide both into place, then tap the warmer.
pages.why: Higher up the thermometer is warmer. −5 °C is 5 below zero and −18 °C is 18 below, so −18 °C sits much lower and −5 °C is warmer.

pages.alt: An upright number line from 1 down to minus 2, marked in quarters. Minus 1/2 is marked halfway from 0 down to minus 1. Minus 1.5 is marked halfway from minus 1 down to minus 2.

pages.text: Fractions and decimals go below zero too. −1/2 sits halfway from 0 down to −1. −1.5 sits halfway from −1 down to −2.

pages.name: Find −3/4
pages.task: In Fractions you put 3/4 on a line. Now tap where −3/4 goes.
pages.why: Below zero, count quarters down from 0. Three quarter-steps down land on −3/4, one quarter short of −1.

pages.task: Your meter reads −12.0 V across a battery. Why the minus?
pages.why: On DC, a meter shows a minus when its leads are the other way round. Swap them back and it reads 12.0 V, the opposite of −12.0 V.

pages.name: Smallest to biggest
pages.task: Tap these from smallest to biggest.
pages.why: Smallest is lowest on the line. −2 is lowest, then −3/4, then −0.5, which is −1/2. 1 is above zero, so it is the biggest.
